Position that maps track values into a radial band

Source: R/geom-track.R
position_track.Rd

Applies the normalisation described in geom_track(). ggplot2 runs a position after the stat and the geom setup, so the layer must already carry y – track_angles() adds it.

Usage

position_track(
  band,
  node = NULL,
  geom_name = NULL,
  anchored = FALSE,
  band_fill = FALSE,
  stack = FALSE,
  scales = c("free", "fixed"),
  limits = NULL,
  baseline = NULL,
  width = 0.9,
  offset = 0
)

Arguments

band

Track name or c(r0, r1) radius interval. A name can only be resolved inside a ggcircos() plot (the layout declares the bands); standalone use needs the numeric form.

node

Name of the node id column; only used to group stacks.

geom_name

Name of the track geometry.

anchored

Stretch from the band's inner edge (default FALSE).

band_fill

Fill the whole band radially (xmin = r0, xmax = r1) instead of scaling a value into it. Set by geom_track() for "tile".

stack, scales, limits, baseline, width, offset

See geom_track().

Value

A ggplot2 position.

Details

The position holds plain vectors only (band, the normalisation settings, the node column name) – never a layout or a node table, so one position object can be shared by several layers without them seeing each other's data (spec sec.8.2).

Examples

# the escape hatch: reuse the normalisation on any geom
set.seed(1)
d <- track_angles(
    data.frame(id = "mpg", value = runif(10)),
    "id", circos_layout(cor(mtcars)), 0.9, "point"
)
ggcircos(cor(mtcars), order = "hclust", tracks = c(values = 0.2)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = d,
        ggplot2::aes(x = value, y = y),
        position = position_track(band = c(1.06, 1.26), anchored = TRUE),
        inherit.aes = FALSE
    )
